topic: Disjunctive threshold-cut sensitivity analysis for ordinal survivor-complier benefit under joint relaxations of treatment and selection monotonicity. With randomized binary assignment Z, binary received treatment D, exclusion and consistency, finite-support X, and finite ordinal Y observed only when S=1, allow all four compliance types. Bound aggregate defier mass by delta_D and, among compliers, bound the covariate-aggregated minority of the two opposing selection-response types by delta_S. Target the sharp set of P(Y(1)>Y(0) | D(0)=0,D(1)=1,S(0)=S(1)=1). PROVED SUBFIELD SCOPE: Compatible full laws project exactly onto a finite union of orientation-specific rational threshold-cut polytopes, and every complete reduced point lifts to a compatible full response law. Each fixed orientation branch has O(|X|K) extended size; the full union may contain up to 2^|X| branches, so no branch-free scalable positive-budget algorithm is claimed. Whenever the positive-denominator target exists, its sharp set is an attained interval with bounded-support endpoint laws. Observable orientation screening yields exact pointwise endpoint computation by at most 2^(r_amb+1) rational linear programs for r_amb ambiguous cells. For rational observed masses, exhaustive enumeration of all orientations and full-rank active bases gives a finite exact semialgebraic stratification, including singular and lower-dimensional strata, with separate model-infeasible, model-feasible/target-empty, and target-nonempty labels and rational endpoint formulas only on target-nonempty strata. The stratification also supports pointwise-relative conclusion-boundary labels and, for rational q, radial direction, and threshold, exact feasibility-entry, target-entry, and critical-budget reports by finite univariate root isolation. A simultaneous finite-sample outer confidence surface follows by projection of a multinomial primitive region. ACCEPTED-BOUNDARY POSITIONING: At delta_D=delta_S=0, the construction recovers the branch-free no-defier, covariate-wise one-sided-selection partial-transport projection, ordinal cuts, full-law lifting, sharp endpoints, and sparse O(|X|K) threshold-flow computation already proved in accepted-bank pid_slate_benefit_partialtransport_v1. The present contribution is the positive-budget disjunctive extension with unknown diagonal residuals and defiers, possible coexistence of opposing selection responses within cells, and aggregate-budget coupling of survivor mass. OPEN QUESTION, NOT A BANKED RESULT OR PRACTICAL DELIVERABLE: A degeneracy-safe output-sensitive symbolic endpoint-chart enumerator remains unproved. The available all-bases construction proves finite exact existence but may inspect exponentially many infeasible, singular, duplicate, or nonoptimal bases that emit no chart. No complexity bound charged only to emitted charts and certificates, no rejected-basis audit, and no scalable component-discovery guarantee is claimed. The earlier proposed early-kill test for that practical enumerator is undischarged and remains part of the open question, not evidence for a completed algorithm. The Job Corps and Oregon encouragement designs provide variable-level motivation only; no empirical reanalysis or transfer of published numerical bounds is claimed.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the sharp identified set for the ordinal probability of strict benefit among always-selected compliers when both treatment monotonicity and selection monotonicity may fail, with defier mass bounded by delta_D and the covariate-aggregated minority selection orientation among compliers bounded by delta_S.

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp intensive-margin complier-effect bounds with endogenous treatment and weak sample-selection monotonicity, but not simultaneous bounded failures of treatment and selection monotonicity or ordinal benefit.
source_refs.author: Yingying Dong and Phillip Heiler

source_refs.claim: Derives sharp symbolic bounds for ordinal probabilities of benefit in imperfect randomized studies, including formulas with and without no-defiers, but has no truncation-by-selection principal stratum.
source_refs.author: Erin E. Gabriel, Michael C. Sachs, and Andreas Kryger Jensen

source_refs.claim: Treats noncompliance and sample selection jointly for average effects among always-employed compliers under monotonicity and mean-dominance assumptions.
source_refs.author: Xuan Chen and Carlos A. Flores

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest literatures separate the ingredients: Dong–Heiler and Chen–Flores target mean intensive-margin effects while maintaining treatment-monotonicity structure, whereas Gabriel–Sachs–Jensen handles ordinal benefit and defiers without a second post-treatment selection stratum. Once both monotonicities can fail, each observed (Z,D,S,X,Y) cell mixes compliance type, selection orientation, and unobserved ordinal potential-outcome couplings; the target is also a ratio whose denominator can vanish. Sharpness therefore requires orientation-specific latent allocations, denominator-zero handling, and a constructive full-law lifting argument that neither trimming nor ordinary ordinal transportation bounds provides.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact projection-and-lifting characterization of the compatible values of Pr{Y(1)>Y(0) | D(0)=0,D(1)=1,S(0)=S(1)=1} as a finite union of orientation-specific rational threshold-cut polytopes, with attained sharp endpoints for every feasible (delta_D,delta_S).

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from randomized assignment to endogenous receipt and selected outcomes, then to intensive-margin complier effects in Job Corps and Oregon.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Random assignment does not ensure treatment receipt -> outcomes remain observed only for a selected subsample -> policy-relevant intensive-margin effects concern always-selected compliers -> simultaneous monotonicity failures require a two-budget ordinal-benefit identified set.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt categorical response-function enumeration and dual symbolic optimization that convert ordinal benefit events into sharp cumulative-cut inequalities, retaining explicit witness distributions for attainability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination has the same strict ordinal-benefit functional, but its feasible marginals must be generated by the joint compliance-selection mixture system.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt semiparametrically efficient orthogonal scores and cross-fitted debiased machine learning for lower and upper intensive-margin bound functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its nuisance structure and always-selected-complier population are closest to the proposed endpoints, although the new map is disjunctive, ordinal, and sensitivity-indexed.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt test inversion for a partially identified fraction-benefiting functional represented by constrained stochastic optimization, including boundary-aware quadratic approximations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies inference machinery for the same ordinal probability-of-benefit object, while the destination replaces randomized marginal constraints with a union of latent principal-stratum polytopes.

open_problems.open_problem: Develop a degeneracy-safe output-sensitive symbolic enumerator for all feasible endpoint charts of the disjunctive rational threshold-cut programs, including singular, tie, vanishing-denominator, and lower-dimensional budget strata.

source_refs.claim: Gives an output-sensitive critical-region enumeration algorithm for multiparametric LCPs with sufficient matrices and lexicographic treatment of degeneracy, but its guarantee is tied to the pLCP critical-domain representation.
source_refs.author: Sebastiano Columbano, Komei Fukuda, and Colin N. Jones

source_refs.claim: Uses lexicographic perturbation to obtain a unique continuous explicit solution over nonoverlapping regions for degenerate multiparametric linear programs.
source_refs.author: Colin N. Jones, Eric C. Kerrigan, and Jan M. Maciejowski

source_refs.claim: Shows why complete sensitivity charts are substantive econometric outputs, but derives them analytically for a smooth two-assumption model rather than by certified disjunctive parametric optimization.
source_refs.author: Matthew A. Masten and Alexandre Poirier

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing output-sensitive algorithms cover sufficient-matrix pLCP critical regions or lexicographically perturbed multiparametric LPs, not a finite union of orientation-specific Charnes–Cooper programs whose feasibility and target denominator both change with two budgets. Perturbing away degeneracy can create regions absent from the unperturbed econometric chart, while enumerating all bases can cause exponential rejected-basis work. Equality strata, empty-target faces, and full-law certificates must be emitted rather than silently discarded, so ordinary basis walking does not establish the required output-sensitive guarantee.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact rational algorithm with a complexity theorem charging polynomial work to the input and the emitted full-dimensional charts, lower-dimensional strata, and infeasibility or empty-target certificates, plus a proof that every budget point receives the correct sharp endpoint label and a liftable full-law witness.

writing_exemplar.why: Its presentation makes the complete sensitivity chart, rather than isolated pointwise optimizations, the object researchers inspect and report.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sensitivity has multiple dimensions -> conclusions vary across the assumption region -> a frontier or chart is the empirical deliverable -> exact disjunctive sharp bounds require certified symbolic chart enumeration.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt adjacency traversal of critical domains, lexicographic perturbation, symbolic Chebyshev-center tests, and LP-oracle complexity accounting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest output-sensitive polyhedral-region enumeration proof, but the destination must quotient perturbed bases into unperturbed rational-value charts and retain lower-dimensional pieces.

method_exemplars.technique: Use symbolic lexicographic perturbation and adjacent-region pivots to resolve primal and dual degeneracy without overlapping full-dimensional cells.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint problems become multiparametric LPs after homogenization, but their output must include singular faces and disjunction labels rather than only a unique optimizer.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a finite-sample simultaneous outer confidence set for the entire two-budget sharp endpoint surface of ordinal survivor-complier benefit, valid across orientation ties, infeasible budgets, and vanishing target denominators.

source_refs.claim: Provides pointwise-consistent confidence intervals for an ordinal fraction benefiting in a randomized trial and identifies missing outcomes as a future extension.
source_refs.author: Emily J. Huang, Ethan X. Fang, Daniel F. Hanley, and Michael Rosenblum

source_refs.claim: Provides uniformly asymptotically valid calibrated-projection intervals for smooth functions or components of moment-inequality parameters using repeated feasibility problems.
source_refs.author: Hiroaki Kaido, Francesca Molinari, and Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Bootstraps value functions of perturbed linear programs for uniformly valid inference on scalar functionals of sets defined by linear moments.
source_refs.author: JoonHwan Cho and Thomas M. Russell

open_problems.why_unsolved: Huang et al. treat one benefit functional in a complete-outcome randomized trial, while projection and perturbed-LP methods are asymptotic and generally target one subvector or functional at a time. The desired object is a set-valued surface indexed by a continuum of (delta_D,delta_S), with discontinuous feasibility labels and nonregular changes in active orientation and denominator. Pointwise intervals or a bootstrap at one budget do not ensure simultaneous coverage, especially at orientation ties and zero-probability observed cells.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence-set construction projecting an exact or conservative finite-sample multinomial region for all observable cell probabilities through every orientation-specific latent-law program, with a proof that the resulting random lower and upper surface encloses the population sharp surface simultaneously with probability at least 1-alpha.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference through the clinically interpretable fraction benefiting and highlights the nonregular constrained-optimization obstacle.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Average effects hide individual benefit -> the fraction benefiting is partially identified -> endpoint uncertainty is nonregular -> truncation, noncompliance, and a sensitivity surface require simultaneous rather than pointwise coverage.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over test inversion for the ordinal benefit probability and its boundary-aware constrained stochastic-optimization proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It targets the same causal functional, but the destination confidence object must project through compliance-selection mixtures and cover all sensitivity budgets jointly.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt calibrated projection and feasibility-based inversion to eliminate high-dimensional latent response-law variables while preserving coverage of the projected target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The sharp endpoint is a projection of a partially identified latent vector, although finite-sample multinomial coverage can replace asymptotic calibration.

method_exemplars.technique: Use randomly perturbed LP value functions to stabilize inference at optimal-basis changes and prove uniform validity under linear moment restrictions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Each orientation-specific homogenized endpoint is an LP value function, but simultaneous union and denominator-degeneracy handling remain unresolved.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize the exact feasible two-budget region and its falsification and breakdown frontiers for conclusions about survivor-complier ordinal benefit when defiers and opposing selection types are jointly permitted.

source_refs.claim: Defines and estimates breakdown frontiers for conclusions including a minimum fraction benefiting under simultaneous relaxations of two assumptions, but without principal-stratum selection.
source_refs.author: Matthew A. Masten and Alexandre Poirier

source_refs.claim: Develops LATE breakdown frontiers under joint relaxations of IV independence and no-defiers, but does not include truncation-by-selection or ordinal individual benefit.
source_refs.author: Pedro Picchetti

source_refs.claim: Characterizes falsification frontiers and adaptive sets for relaxed IV models, providing a template for separating model feasibility from target conclusions.
source_refs.author: Matthew A. Masten and Alexandre Poirier

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing breakdown-frontier work typically keeps the target well-defined throughout the relaxation region. Here the always-selected-complier denominator can be zero, and observed cells can force, exclude, or leave ambiguous the selection-response orientation. Model feasibility, nonemptiness of the target stratum, and the conclusion Pr{benefit}>=c therefore have distinct frontiers. Joint latent-mass budgets also create disjunctive orientation regimes rather than one smooth frontier, so standard continuous-relaxation arguments do not supply exact labels or certificates.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A finite piecewise-rational characterization of the feasible-budget set, positive-denominator subset, and breakdown frontier for every threshold conclusion Pr{benefit}>=c, with observable orientation screens and primal or dual certificates for infeasible and empty-target regions.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies a conclusion-first motivation for a multidimensional assumption-relaxation chart and explicitly considers proportion-benefiting conclusions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Empirical conclusions rest on multiple assumptions -> relaxations should be indexed and ordered -> identified sets determine where a conclusion survives -> survivor-complier benefit needs a frontier that also labels feasibility and target existence.

method_exemplars.technique: Define the robust region as a level set of a sharp endpoint map and derive the frontier as its boundary while separating identification from inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is a two-assumption breakdown chart, but its endpoint map comes from a disjunctive principal-stratum ratio program.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt sample-analogue frontier estimation and bootstrap inference for an IV sensitivity surface with a defier-share relaxation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already treats defier mass as one frontier coordinate; the destination adds a selection-orientation budget and a partially observed ordinal target.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the distinction among falsification frontiers, pointwise identified sets, and frontier-adaptive sets using explicit feasibility certificates.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination must distinguish incompatible budgets from compatible budgets whose survivor-complier stratum is empty, refining standard falsification-frontier logic.

literature_map:
1. Dong and Heiler (2026, arXiv:2606.09223) is the closest destination anchor: sharp intensive-margin complier bounds, orthogonal DML, and Job Corps/Oregon applications under weak selection monotonicity.
2. Chen and Flores (2015, JBES) jointly address noncompliance and sample selection for average effects among always-employed compliers while maintaining monotonicity and mean dominance.
3. Lee (2009, Review of Economic Studies) supplies the foundational trimming argument for selected means; its one-direction selection monotonicity is precisely one assumption being relaxed here.
4. Semenova (2025, Journal of Econometrics; arXiv:2008.12720) allows covariate-dependent selection direction and high-dimensional inference, but not an aggregated minority-of-opposite-types budget.
5. Imai (2007 working paper; 2008 Statistics & Probability Letters) combines noncompliance and truncation-by-death through principal-stratum and contaminated-distribution bounds under classical monotonicity structure.
6. Gabriel, Sachs, and Jensen (2024, Biometrika; arXiv:2305.10555) give symbolic sharp ordinal-benefit bounds in imperfect randomized trials, with and without no-defiers, but no selection-defined target stratum.
7. Lu, Ding, and Dasgupta (2018, Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics; DOI 10.3102/1076998618776435) establish sharp bounds for probabilities of benefit and strict benefit from ordinal marginals.
8. Huang, Fang, Hanley, and Rosenblum (2019, Biometrics) develop constrained-optimization inference for the ordinal fraction benefiting and explicitly flag missing outcomes as a future extension.
9. Masten and Poirier (2020, Quantitative Economics; arXiv:1705.04765) provide the two-assumption breakdown-frontier template and include fraction-benefiting conclusions, but not latent survivor-complier ratios.
10. Picchetti (2026, arXiv:2603.25529) studies joint IV-independence and no-defier relaxations for LATE, while omitting selection monotonicity.
11. Lafférs (2017, Economics Letters; DOI 10.1016/j.econlet.2017.06.039) formulates Lee-bound sensitivity as LP optimization under simultaneous treatment-exogeneity and selection-monotonicity deviations, but not joint compliance-type and survivor-type budgets.
12. Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019, Econometrica) and Cho and Russell (2024, JBES) provide projection and perturbed-LP inference tools, both asymptotic rather than exact finite-sample surface coverage.
13. Columbano, Fukuda, and Jones (2009, arXiv:0807.2318) and Jones, Kerrigan, and Maciejowski (2007, Automatica) are the closest symbolic-parametric optimization donors for output-sensitive traversal and degeneracy handling.
14. Blanco, Chen, Flores, and Flores-Lagunes (2020, JBES) derive sharp duration mean and quantile bounds under censoring, selection, and noncompliance, but retain monotonicity or stochastic-dominance restrictions.
15. The unoccupied intersection is ordinal individual benefit, always-selected complier targeting, and simultaneous bounded treatment and selection monotonicity failures; the main obstacles are disjunctive orientations, ratio denominators, nonregular chart boundaries, and certified sharp lifting.
